headline: What the postponed fixed admission period rule would change for students
plain: In July 2026, the Department of Homeland Security published a rule to replace duration of status with a fixed period of admission for F, J, and I visa holders. Under it, an F or J stay would run to the program end date, up to 4 years, plus 30 days to depart. The time to prepare to depart after study or practical training would drop from 60 to 30 days. A court in Boston has put off the start of the rule.

claims.text: The final rule (FR Doc. 2026-14439) changes the admission period in the F, J, and I classifications from duration of status to an admission for a fixed time period.
claims.quote: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) is amending its regulations to change the admission period in the F, J, and I classifications from duration of status to an admission for a fixed time period

claims.text: Under the final rule, admission is granted up to the program end date, not to exceed 4 years, plus 30 days for F and J nonimmigrants to depart.
claims.quote: Upon admission into the United States, a fixed period of stay is granted up to the program end date, not to exceed 4 years, plus an additional 30-days for F and J nonimmigrants to depart.

claims.text: The final rule decreases the period for F-1 nonimmigrants to prepare to depart after a course of study or post-completion practical training from 60 to 30 days.
claims.quote: Decreasing the period allowed for F-1 nonimmigrants to prepare to depart from the United States after completion of a course of study or an authorized period of post-completion practical training from 60 to 30 days

claims.text: The final rule set its effective date as September 15, 2026.
The District of Massachusetts (No. 1:26-cv-13799, ECF 51) postponed the effective date of the final rule on September 14, 2026, until the court orders otherwise or decides the merits.
claims.quote: The effective date of the Final Rule is hereby POSTPONED pending further order of this court or resolution of this proceeding on the merits.

history.note: Final rule published at 91 FR 44976, effective date September 15, 2026.
The District of Massachusetts postponed the effective date and enjoined implementation (ECF 51).
